question.text: Which AIF investments are most exposed to higher mortality risk and the J Curve's early negative phase?

answer.text: Listed-market hedge funds with frequent rebalancing
Category I VCF investments in early-stage unlisted ventures
Category II debt funds with senior-secured exposures
All AIF categories share identical lifecycle return profiles

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports a Category I/VCF focus on early-stage unlisted ventures with higher mortality risk and the J Curve mechanics for AIF fund lifecycles. Early-stage VCF investments are therefore most exposed to early negative J Curve behaviour and investee failure risk. The Trap: Category III hedge-fund discussion is outside the workbook's scope, so cross-category J Curve comparisons are not source-backed. Debt funds and "identical across categories" are not what the source describes. Note: Earlier wording compared J Curve "depth" across categories and added 5-10 year timing, -20% to -30% early returns, and debt-fund and hedge-fund J Curve claims. Those are not directly sourced and have been removed; only the early-stage Category I/VCF mortality and AIF J Curve points remain.
